analysis.title: 2027 Global Economics Outlook: Powered by AI, Tested by Oil
key_insights: Baseline: global growth stays solid at about 3.4% in 2027-28, with the US supported by AI capex and wealth-driven consumption by high-income households. Growth softens modestly in 2027 and recovers in 2028.

Inflation has been persistent after the energy shock. MS expects headline and core inflation to peak around 1Q27 and core to approach central bank targets by 4Q28. The call relies on energy prices continuing to fall.
Developed-market central banks begin a modest hiking cycle. Policy rates peak in 1Q27 (Fed 4.25-4.5%, ECB 3.0%, BoJ 1.75%), then a modest cutting cycle in 2028. Fed cuts begin 2Q28 to 3.625%.

Crude on screens is no longer a sufficient statistic. Refining spreads are historically wide and commodity strategists expect diesel to stay tight into mid-2027. Europe feels this most and Asia least.

AI capex: hyperscaler capex is forecast at $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028. 5GW of US projects shift from 2028 to 2029, leaving US data center capex flat 2027-28. AI contribution to US growth peaks around 2027.

Imports reduce AI's direct GDP contribution. In 3Q26 AI investment added 1.6pp before imports and 0.9pp after. AI-linked goods are nearly one-quarter of US imports, which supports Taiwan, Korea, Mexico and the wider Asia capex cycle.

AI productivity so far reflects capital deepening, not broad TFP gains. Trend US productivity is 2.1% and the baseline assumes 2.3% by 2028. AI displacement is micro rather than macro, with an estimated 15bp or less added to unemployment through 1H26.

Real neutral rate in the US is estimated near 1.5%, up from just below 1% in early 2025, so policy is neutral to modestly restrictive. A sustained productivity gain would lift r*, which makes the case for a higher neutral stronger than confidence in its exact level.

Europe has the strongest inflation persistence. Euro area headline peaks above 4% in early 2027 (4.0% in October). The ECB hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027 to 3.0%, holds until June 2028, then cuts to 2.25%.
BoJ hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027 to 1.75% and then pauses. BoE hikes in Dec and Feb to 4.5% and holds through 2027. RBA is at its 4.85% peak with cuts expected in Aug and Nov 2027.

Scenario analysis: Aggregate Demand upside takes the Fed to 5.625%. AI Productivity upside holds the Fed at 4.375% with faster growth and less inflation. AI Investment downside takes unemployment above 5% and the Fed to 1.375%. Rates and Oil downside has oil at $125-150, a mild US recession and the Fed at 5.375% on the report's own text.

Emerging markets face stronger inflation. RBI hikes to 6.25% by April 2027, Brazil holds at 13.75% through 2027, Banxico makes a final cut to 6.0% in March 2027, and China holds rates at 1.25% amid lowflation.

Fiscal: US deficit stays near 6% of GDP, debt about 125%. France is the pressure point, with debt heading toward about 160% by 2040 and April 2027 elections. UK consolidates. Japan debt ratio has fallen six straight years on strong nominal growth.

Policy and trade: MS sees scope for marginally higher tariffs post mid-terms, USMCA review as a key catalyst, and US-China managed competition with Busan consensus items expiring in early January. AI data center restrictions are a state-level delay story, not a federal pause.

Asia: Taiwan 2026 GDP forecast raised to 13.5% and 8.7% in 2027, Korea 3.0% in 2027, China 4.4% in 2027 with nominal growth slowing. Saudi Arabia contracts 1.6% in 2026 and rebounds 6.4% in 2027 on oil normalization.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex is the key US growth driver and supports Asian exporters, though the growth rate slows after 2027.
Diesel tightness and wide refining spreads hurt Europe most and raise second-round inflation risk.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Two 25bp hikes in Dec and Mar, then a hold through 2027 and 75bp of cuts in 2028.
Policy is described as neutral to modestly restrictive.
Hikes in December and March, hold until June 2028, then cuts to 2.25% by 4Q28.
Two hikes then a pause through 2028.
Resilient growth supports the hiking bias.
Reluctant disinflation keeps the Fed focused on second-round effects.
The October figure is released and the early 2027 peak is a forecast.
Stable global growth despite energy and tighter policy.

macro_indicators.indicator: Oil price in Rates and Oil downside scenario
macro_indicators.interpretation: Stagflation and a mild US recession in late 2027.
Slow-hire slow-fire labor market with no overheating.

risk_factors: Energy shock could turn nonlinear, with energy, food and supply-chain pressure passing into core inflation.
AI capex shortfall or delay would cut US growth, hit asset prices and spill to Asia and Europe via exports.
Repeated supply shocks may shift inflation expectations and force more demand restriction.
Aggregate demand overheating could force the Fed to 5.625%.
Fiscal risks: France deficit not consolidating, US reliance on bills, Brazil fiscal uncertainty, and gilt market constraints.
Tariff re-escalation, USMCA outcome and export controls could delay investment.
Neutral rate estimates may be biased upward by supply shocks, risking overtightening.
charts_described: Exhibit 20: hyperscaler capex estimates of 155, 157, 262, 481, 951, 1641 and 1760 bn USD for 2022-2028.
Exhibit 10: AI-related contributions to US growth over 1pp in 2026-2028 per the exhibit caption.
Exhibit 76: Asia nominal exports with early reporters accounting for 58% of Asia's nominal exports in USD.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict remains unresolved, though commodity strategists and market pricing point to de-escalation. Renewed hostilities are the Rates and Oil downside scenario.

US-China: Busan consensus has three components expiring in early January (178 Section 301 exclusions, BIS Affiliates Rule suspension, China's second-wave rare-earth controls). Base case is extension. Watch the NDAA and MATCH Act.
USMCA review and Sec. 232 are key catalysts for tariffs on Mexico and Canada.
French presidential election on 18 April and 2 May 2027, with possible June parliamentary elections. Spain and Italy also face elections.
US mid-term elections produced a divided Congress, with little expected change in executive-driven tariff policy.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex rises to $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028, and AI productivity upside could lift growth with less inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth rate of capex slows sharply, 5GW slips to 2029, and an outright spending fall would push US unemployment above 5% and the Fed to 1.375%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI investment falling outright in 2027 due to power and construction bottlenecks.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil moves lower in line with market pricing, headline inflation peaks in 1Q27 and central banks stop after a brief tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: Diesel stays tight into mid-2027 and second-round effects could force more tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hostilities in the Middle East resume and oil rises to $125-150/bbl.

theme_stances.key_argument: Central banks anticipate inflation pressure by tightening into the new year, with policy peaking in 1Q27 before easing in 2028.
